text: One song is played at every wedding in your nation. What is it about, and why do the grandparents wince?
Your coins carry a face or a symbol that people argue about. What is it, and who wants it replaced?
Does your nation have conscription? Say who serves, who gets out of it, and how.
Your second city insists it should be the first. What does it have that the capital doesn't?
What do people in your nation queue for without complaint, and what would start a riot if they had to queue for it?
A civil servant has held the same desk for forty years and outlasted eleven ministers. What do they know?
A region of your nation votes against the government every single time. What does it want that it never gets?
Your nation once lost a war it still calls a draw. What did the peace really cost?
Your national dish started as poor people's food. What is in it, and who serves the expensive version now?
There is something your nation has to import and hates importing. What is it, and who sells it?
Your army's most decorated regiment is recruited from a single region. Why there, and what does the region expect in return?
There is a corner of your nation that every map shows and almost nobody visits. What is out there, and who lives there anyway?
A child in your nation turns sixteen. What are they suddenly allowed to do, and what is still three years away?
Name the journalist your government fears most. What story are they sitting on?
Your head of state has one power they have never dared to use. What would have to happen first?
An old family name still opens doors in your nation. What did that family do, and how long ago?
A sport nobody else takes seriously fills stadiums in your nation. Which rule does a foreigner never understand?
A town in your nation was built around one industry, and the industry has just closed. What happens to the town?
Your nation keeps a military base far from home. What deal put it there, and who thinks it was a bad one?
A mountain pass, a strait or a bridge: pick the one place your nation cannot afford to lose. What happens on the day it closes?
Who is the leader of your nation, and how did they get into power?
What are the most famous ruins in your nation? What were they in their glory days, and why are they in ruin?
How do the people of your nation spend the days when they are not working? How long is the weekend, and who gets it off?
How do your people prefer to get around? How does it differ between the city and the countryside?
How long have your people known peace? How has war, or the lack of it, shaped your modern history?
What are your nation's famous cities, apart from the capital, and what makes each unlike the others?
Do your people gather for three meals a day, or follow another arrangement? Which is the largest meal?
I am reading through your nation's history books. Which names am I sure to come across?
In a leader, what do the people of your nation value most: strength, kindness or good sense? Who was the last leader to have it?
Which landmark in your nation was built by an ancient culture for reasons nobody now knows? What is the favourite theory?
What are the best-known folk stories in your nation? Who brings good fortune, and who is the bogeyman parents scare their children with?
What forms of gambling are legal in your nation? Who controls the gambling scene, and what does the public think of it?
How many branches do your armed forces have, and which formation in them is the most famous?
What are the most important regions of your nation? What makes their people stand out from the rest?
What does an average household look like in your nation? Who lives under one roof, and do the pets live inside?
Who is considered the founding father or mother of your modern nation, and what do people prefer to forget about them?
Which political parties exist in your nation, what divides them, and how do they work together?
What skills or trades from your nation's history have died out? Is anyone trying to revive them?
What is the traditional formal wear of your nation, and what do people wear to relax? Which outfit might be called the national dress?
What are the most common recreational drugs in your nation, and which of them are legal?
Describe a day in the life of an ordinary soldier in training in your nation.
Which body of water is the most indispensable in your nation? How has access to water, or the lack of it, featured in your history?
What about weddings in your nation: who officiates, where are they held, and how many people are invited?
Who is the most renowned celebrity in your nation, and what are they famous for?
Describe an election day in your nation. Who votes, where, and how long before anyone knows the result?
Are your people the original inhabitants of your nation's lands, or did they displace another group? Who remembers it differently?
What sorts of headgear do people wear in your nation, and why: use, ceremony or prestige?
What are the railways like in your nation? Are they part of a wider network, or cut off by gauge, geography or politics?
Who are the most feared enemies in your nation's history, and are they still feared?
How is the ownership of land divided in your nation? Are there lands beyond your borders that your people still call theirs?
What rituals are observed when someone dies in your nation? What happens to the body, and how are the dead honoured?
Who is making the big money in your nation? What is the difference between the old rich and the newly rich?
Is your civil service efficient and open to talent, or a bloated system of patronage? Say how someone really gets a job in it.
Give the synopsis of your people's national epic. Which part does everyone know by heart?
What sort of music is popular in your nation? Is there a genre your nation created or made its own?
What is your nation's largest export, and who would be ruined if the world stopped buying it?
Which battle does your nation remember above all others? Who fought it, why, and how was it won?
What is the weather like in your nation, and how have your people adapted to it? Which natural disaster do they fear most?
What do sick people do in your nation if they want to get better? Who can afford it?
A complex series of murders is beyond the ordinary police. Who is sent to solve the case, and will they find the killer?
A thief steals a visitor's wallet in one of your cities. Who do they report it to, and what will be done about it?
What is the closest your nation has come to being wiped out, and what saved it?
What do your people consider to be art, and what do they refuse to call art?
What is the currency of your nation? How did it come to be used, and what came before it?
Describe the uniforms of your armed forces. What does a soldier wear on parade that would be useless in the field?
What does an ordinary public park look like in your nation? Is there wilderness left, and who protects it?
It is late at night in your nation and a visitor is hungry. What is still open?
A great calamity strikes your nation: fire, flood or earthquake. Who is sent to clean up and repair, and who gets the credit?
Can the courts strike down laws in your nation? Why, or why not?
From knights of virtue to pirates of the high seas: what kind of people has your nation romanticised, and what were they really like?
When do your people celebrate the new year, and what does it involve?
Where does the drinking water come from in your nation, and how does it reach the tap?
Who guards your head of state? Describe the guard, its uniform and its oldest privilege.
Tourists travel from one end of your nation to the other. Which five natural wonders do they stop for?
How have pets shaped the life of your people? Which animals are kept by which kind of household?
Astronaut, firefighter, doctor: what do children in your nation dream of becoming? And the adults?
What are the gun laws of your nation, and who wants them changed?
What is the most sought-after lost treasure of your nation's past, and who is still looking for it?
What makes people laugh in your nation: dry wit, sarcasm, slapstick? Which subjects are never joked about?
What happens to rubbish and sewage in your nation? Where does it all end up?
Which fort or castle in your nation matters most? Who built it, and against whom?
How did your nation decide which city was to be its capital?
Where do young people in your nation go to be with each other, away from their parents?
Who are the itinerant folk of your nation, and why do they travel?
What could be found on your nation's black markets, and who looks the other way?
How did your nation become independent, and from whom?
What symbolism do colours have in your nation's cultures? Which colour would nobody wear to a wedding?
What do your nation's farmers grow, and which crop pays the bills?
Where does your nation stand on nuclear weapons? Who decided, and when?
I have spent some time in your capital and decide to travel to the countryside. How different is life there?
A visitor has decided to settle in your nation. How do they obtain a house?
Tell us about one of your nation's secret societies. Who is rumoured to belong?
What is the single greatest threat your nation faces today: nature, politics or unrest? Who is paid to worry about it?
What is considered the darkest day in your nation's history, and how is it remembered?
Which film was the latest box office success in your nation? What was it about, and why was it so popular?
How wide is the gap between rich and poor in your nation? What catches those who fall on hard times?
How are veterans treated after their service in your nation: honoured, or forgotten?
What lies beneath your nation: caves, underground rivers, old mines? Does anyone live or work down there?
How does a parcel or a message get from one place to another in your nation?
What subcultures do rebellious young people join in your nation, and what do their parents make of it?
What is your prison system for, rehabilitation or punishment? Describe an ordinary day inside.
How is history taught in your nation? Name one accepted truth that is actually a lie.
Does your government fund the arts? If so, what strings come attached?
How easy is it to start a business in your nation? Name what stands in the way.
Is your nation's military technology its own invention, or bought and borrowed? Name the weapon it is proudest of.
What does the night sky look like from your nation, and what do your people call the shapes they see in it?
Where do people in your nation get their news, and do they believe it?
Who are your nation's major artists, and what are they known for?
Who is your nation's closest ally, and why? What would it take to end the friendship?
What is the great 'what if' of your nation's history? How would things be different had it gone the other way?
Give a proverb or two from your nation. What do they say about the people who use them?
Beyond the black market, what does the grey economy look like in your nation: street vendors, cash in hand, favours? How large is it?
Does your nation have an intelligence agency? Name its most famous success, and the failure it never mentions.
What does a city street in your nation smell and sound like, compared with a village or a forest?
What are some common names in your nation, and why are they popular?
Who are the star players of your national sport, and which rivalry divides the country?
What is the most significant foreign policy goal of your current government, and which neighbour stands in its way?
Describe a civil war in your nation's past. Who fought whom, and is it really over?
How do your people think the world began, and how do they think it will end?
I am searching for work in your nation. Where could I apply, where would I apply, and where should I?
What are the ranks in your armed forces, and which rank does the real work?
What landscapes are found in your nation, and which of them are rare anywhere else?
What are the generations of your nation called, and how do they get along?
A foreign student wants to study in your nation. Which university would they hope for, and where would they actually end up?
Describe the buildings your government sits in. Which of them was built to impress, and whom?
How are your nation's historical traumas taught to each new generation?
What sort of architecture can a visitor expect in your nation? Describe a palace, a place of worship and a railway station.
Which nations are your major trading partners, and why do they matter?
Which tactics gave your nation its greatest advantages in battle?
Describe the most beautiful valley in your nation, or the most hellish one.
What are the rites of passage in a person's life in your nation, from birth to death, and how are they marked?
Who makes the food in your nation: who grows it, who cooks it, and who is thanked for it?
What powers does your police force have, and what holds it back?
What role have plagues played in your nation's history, and what did the last one change for good?
What is the best food to eat in each region of your nation?
Which building materials are at hand in your nation, and how have they dictated the look of its towns?
Which military thinker or doctrine has most inspired your nation's way of war?
Name the greatest river of your nation and the ports along it.
How has life in your nation changed in the past ten years, and what do people miss?
Who are the official historians of your nation, and who pays them?
Which international organisations is your nation a member of, and which one would it leave tomorrow if it could?
How do your nation's most important holidays reflect its historical triumphs and its traumas?
What is the biggest, most beloved celebration of the year in your nation? I am invited: what should I wear?
Are your nation's banks centralised or independent? Whom do ordinary people trust with their savings?
Which ship is the pride of your navy, and what is she known for?
Name your nation's islands, from the greatest to the smallest. Which one do mainlanders joke about?
How are children treated in your nation? Until what age are they children, and may they work?
Who controls the media in your nation? Name the owner, editor or minister whom every journalist is careful about.
Who are your nation's allies and who are its enemies? Which of them used to be the other?
A treaty your nation signed generations ago still binds it. What did it give away, and who wants it torn up?
What is the most distinctive symbol of your nation, the one most likely to be recognised abroad?
Is there financial regulation in your nation, or is cronyism the standard practice?
What is the social standing of your armed forces? Would a family be proud or worried to see a child enlist?
Which are the major mountain ranges of your nation, and what do they keep apart?
What are the days, weeks and months called in your nation, and how did they get their names?
Who has more power in your nation, the political leaders or the religious ones? Name the two people who matter most.
How does someone immigrate to your nation? Describe the paperwork, the wait and the part nobody warns them about.
Your nation once had a different name. Why was it changed, and who still uses the old one?
What are the different religions in your nation, and how do they treat each other?
What are your nation's main sources of revenue from industry, and which of them is in trouble?
What do your generals want for the future of the armed forces that they will not get?
How does the balance between civilisation and nature hold up in your nation? Does one overwhelm the other?
What slang would a visitor hear in your nation, and which region or group does it give away?
Does a nobility or other elite exist in your nation? What makes someone one of them, and do they mix with everyone else?
How does your nation's main religion influence its laws and government?
A year is missing from your nation's official history. What happened in it?
How do people worship in your nation? Describe an ordinary service, and what a stranger would get wrong.
What share of your people work on the land, in factories and in offices? How fast is that changing?
Which civic rituals does your government observe in wartime, and which in peace?
Where are your nation's deposits of valuable natural resources, and how has the hunt for them shaped those regions?
What is on the standard school curriculum in your nation, and what is every child taught that a foreigner would find strange?
How much of a career can a writer have in your nation? Name one who made it, and what it cost them.
How do your nation's founding myths turn up in the speeches of its politicians today?
Your nation's oldest law is still in force. What does it say, and when was it last used?
What are the greatest sins in your nation, and who decides?
What is the most valuable material in your nation, and how is it used?
How have mountains, deserts or seas shaped your nation's military history and strategy?
Which are the most expensive and the poorest districts of your capital? What does a visitor notice on crossing from one to the other?
What kills and injures people most often in your nation, and how easy is it to see a doctor?
Tell us something about the organised crime in your nation. Who runs it, and who owes them a favour?
Is there discrimination or segregation in your nation? If so, how do those who defend it justify it?
An invention your nation claims as its own is claimed by a neighbour too. What is it, and who is right?
What do your people believe happens after death, and who is promised the best of it?
Does your economic system reinforce the class structure of your nation, or challenge it?
Your armed forces were last used at home, not abroad. Against whom, and who gave the order?
Where are the best trade ports in your nation, and what made them so?
How does your nation treat illness of the mind: as something to be treated, or as a source of shame?
What are the largest minority groups in your nation? Name someone from one of them whom the whole country knows.
Is there a free press in your nation, or does the state decide what is news?
Your nation's borders were drawn by someone who never saw them. Who, and what did they get wrong?
Can you give a linguistic overview of your nation: which languages are spoken where, and which one do strangers use with each other?
How do the roles expected of men and women affect the kinds of jobs people do in your nation?
A single weapon in your arsenal costs more than a hospital. What is it, and has it ever been used?
What do hunters and anglers go after in your nation, and who regulates them?
Can you give an overview of your nation's most popular drinks? Who drinks what, and when?
Tell us about a famous dynasty or family in your nation, and its black sheep.
How are those who do not follow the main religion viewed and treated in your nation?
A revolution in your nation's past failed. What did the losers want, and which of their demands came true anyway?
Is a traditional art form in your nation losing out to a new entertainment? What does the quarrel say about the country?
Your nation's biggest employer is the state. Which jobs exist only to keep people employed?
Your nation's military academy turns out more officers than there are posts. Where do the rest end up?
Where do your nation's citizens go on holiday, at home and abroad? And who comes to visit them?
When families get together in your nation, which food do they share?
A teacher in a small town has taught three generations of the same families. What does the town owe them?
A law in your nation is broken by almost everyone, every day. Why is it still on the books?
A famine, a fire or a flood is remembered by a single name in your nation. What did the government do, or fail to do?
How is the climate and farming of each region reflected in its traditional cooking?
A product is cheaper across the border, and everyone knows it. What is it, and how does it get home?
One medal in your nation is almost never awarded. What must someone do to earn it, and who was the last?
Which animal or plant is your nation about to lose, and who is trying to save it?
Is there a class system in your society? Can someone born at the bottom reach the top, and how often does it happen?
Your nation's most famous exile has just asked to come home. Who are they, and who would rather they stayed away?
Your capital and your largest city are run by rival parties. What do they fight over?
Your nation's last monarch, or its first president, left office badly. How?
Are there new religious movements or cults in your nation? What do they believe, and what does everyone else make of them?
Your nation's tax office is feared, mocked or ignored. Which, and what did it do to earn it?
Two branches of your armed forces do not get on. What started it, and who pays for the feud?
Which regions of your nation are filling with people, and which are emptying? Why?
Are some jobs or activities reserved for one gender in your nation? Who is quietly ignoring the rule?
The driver of your head of state has heard everything for twenty years. What keeps them quiet?
Your nation's constitution has one article nobody dares to amend. What does it say, and what happened the last time someone tried?
Your nation's founding document is kept behind glass. What is missing from it, and who noticed?
Which holy days does your nation keep, and what happens on the most solemn of them?
Your nation's largest market sells one thing that is not strictly legal. What, and why do the police shop there too?
Your nation's oldest regiment has a mascot, a motto or a custom it will not give up. What is it?
Which is the most impressive building in your nation, and what was it built to prove?
What role do religious communities and foundations play in the daily life of your nation?
Who leads your nation's main faith, and how are they chosen?
A minister in your government has resigned over something small. What was it, and what was it really about?
A city in your nation was once the capital of somewhere else. What is left of that time?
A word in your language cannot be translated. What does it mean, and when is it used?
A strike in your nation shut something down for a month. What, and who gave in first?
A general in your nation's past disobeyed an order and was proved right. What was the order?
One of your nation's borders is a line on a map and nothing on the ground. Who crosses it without noticing?
Everyone in your nation carries one thing in their pocket or bag that a foreigner would not. What is it?
The richest person in your nation started with nothing, or says so. What is the true story?
One town in your nation has had the same mayor for thirty years. How, and who has stopped trying to beat them?
Your nation's oldest university was founded for a purpose it no longer serves. What was it?
What are the holy texts of your nation's religions, and who is allowed to interpret them?
Your nation prints, mints or codes its own money. Who decides how much, and who complains?
Your armed forces train every year for a war they hope never to fight. Against whom?
A road in your nation is closed for half the year. What lies at the end of it, and who lives there through the winter?
Who looks after teeth, eyes and old age in your nation, and where do people turn when the doctors have given up?
A judge in your nation is known for one ruling. What was it, and who has never forgiven them?
Your parliament once sat through the night to pass a single bill. What was so urgent?
A language once spoken in your nation survives only in place names. Who spoke it, and where did they go?
Your nation has a gesture that means the opposite of what foreigners assume. What is it, and who found out the hard way?
One profession in your nation is paid far more than it deserves, and one far less. Which are they?
One piece of your nation's coast, border or airspace is watched more closely than the rest. Why there?
Your capital stands where it does for a reason that no longer applies. What was the reason?
It is the first day of school in your nation. What does a child bring, wear and dread?
Your nation's best-loved athlete lost the one contest that mattered. Why are they loved all the more for it?
An election in your nation was decided by a handful of votes. Which one, and does the losing side still say it was stolen?
A ship, a train or a plane was lost in your nation's past and never found. What was aboard?
Broken down to its essence, what does your nation's biggest religion believe?
A motorway, a dam or an airport in your nation was built for traffic that never came. Who signed it off?
Your nation keeps a reserve of ordinary citizens who could be called up. How many would actually come?
A lake, a forest or a mountain in your nation is said to be cursed, haunted or holy. What do people actually avoid doing there?
Breakfast, second breakfast, elevenses: what are the eating times in your nation?
A whistle-blower in your nation was proved right ten years too late. What became of them?
A protest in your capital has gone on for so long that it has become a landmark. What do the protesters want?
Your nation changed its flag once. What was wrong with the old one, and who still flies it?
A children's rhyme in your nation is about something terrible. What?
People in your nation save for one thing above all others. What is it, and at what age do they give up?
A warship, a tank or an aircraft stands on a plinth in one of your towns. What did it do to earn it?
Your nation's largest city floods, shakes, burns or sinks. Which, and what has it done about it?
A power cut hits your capital for an evening. What do people do, and who was ready for it?
The oldest person in your nation has just had a birthday. What do they remember that nobody else does?
Your nation's smallest party holds the balance of power. What does it ask for, every time?
A king, a president or a general in your past is remembered by a nickname. What is it, and did they earn it?
What do your people find fashionable? What is the latest trend, and which generation hates it?
Your nation's best-known brand is known abroad for the wrong reason. What is it, and what is the reason?
Your nation's soldiers serve abroad under someone else's flag. Where, and what do they write home about?
A village in your nation can only be reached by boat, by rail or on foot. Why has nobody built a road?
How do people behave at meals in your nation, and what would get a guest never invited again?
A foreigner has lived in your nation for forty years and is still called 'the foreigner'. What do they do there?
Your government keeps a list of things that may not be exported. What is the strangest item on it?
Your nation's first railway, road or canal went somewhere odd. Where, and who insisted?
Your national theatre, opera or museum is fighting over one thing in its collection. What is it, and who wants it back?
A whole region of your nation lives off visitors. What do the locals do in the off season?
A military parade is held in your capital once a year. What is shown, and what is kept out of sight?
Two towns in your nation face each other across a river and cannot stand each other. What started it?
People in your nation complain about one public service above all others. Which, and is the complaint fair?
Your nation's most famous criminal is something of a folk hero. What did they steal, and from whom?
A referendum in your nation gave the wrong answer. What was the question, and what did the government do next?
A trial in your nation's past is still argued over. Who was in the dock, and was the verdict just?
Which sports are popular in your nation, and is any of them dangerous enough to worry the authorities?
Your nation subsidises something it cannot afford to. What, and who would riot if it stopped?
Your nation buys its fighter aircraft, rifles or ships from a single supplier. What does the supplier get in return?
Your nation has a place everybody claims to have visited and few have. Where is it, and why do they lie?
What does a pensioner in your nation do on an ordinary Tuesday?
A priest, a doctor and a schoolmaster run a village in your nation between them. Which of the three is really in charge?
Your nation's upper house, council or court is full of people nobody elected. Who put them there, and why is that tolerated?
Your grandparents' generation lived through something they called simply 'the hard years'. What happened?
People in your nation give a particular gift when someone moves house. What is it, and what does it mean to arrive without one?
A family firm in your nation has outlived three governments and two currencies. What does it make?
A mutiny in your nation's history is taught as a heroic act, or not taught at all. Which, and why?
An island, an enclave or a valley in your nation runs on its own rules. Which rules, and who lets it?
A stranger knocks on a door in your nation at dinner time. What happens next?
The head of your central bank said one sentence that moved the markets. What was it?
A census in your nation asks one question that people lie about. Which, and why?
A border your nation once had runs through the middle of a modern town. How can a visitor still tell?
Which holidays does your nation observe, and what is eaten or drunk only on days of celebration?
Shops in your nation close on a particular day or hour that annoys visitors. When, and who defends it?
Your nation's border guards know the smugglers by name. How does that arrangement work?
The wind in your nation has a name. When does it blow, and what is it blamed for?
Renting or owning, flat or house: how does a young couple in your nation find a first home, and who helps pay?
A general in your nation has never fought a war. What are they good at instead?
A scandal ended three careers in your government last year. Who talked?
A book was banned in your nation for a century. What was in it, and who read it anyway?
There is a number, a colour or a day your people consider unlucky. Which, and how far do they go to avoid it?
Your nation's poorest region sits on its richest resource. How did that happen?
A weapon was banned in your nation after a single use. What happened?
A stretch of your nation's coast, steppe or desert is empty on purpose. Who emptied it, and why?
What is on television in your nation at eight in the evening, and who is watching?
Your nation's first woman to hold some high office is still alive. Which office, and what does she say about those who followed?
Your nation's local councils have one power the capital envies. What is it?
Your nation once had colonies, or was one. What is the one word from that time that everybody still uses?
What are the most popular forms of entertainment in your nation: which shows, books or games does everyone know?
One import is taxed so heavily that smuggling it is a trade of its own. What is it?
Your nation's defence ministry occupies a building it has outgrown, or one far too grand. Which, and what does that say?
Your nation's highest point is not its most famous mountain. Which is, and why?
There is one day a year when nobody in your nation works. What do they do instead?
A shopkeeper in your capital has sold to every head of government for decades. What do they know about each?
The national anthem has a verse that is no longer sung. What does it say?
A great building in your nation was never finished. Who ran out of money, patience or time?
One regional accent in your nation is used on stage to mean 'fool'. Whose, and how do they take it?
Your nation's pension age has just changed. Which way, and who was in the streets about it?
A song the soldiers sing is not in any official songbook. What is it about?
One crop, tree or animal is found on your coat of arms and hardly anywhere else. Where did it go?
A neighbour in your nation is too loud, too nosy or too quiet. How is that dealt with?
The most hated referee, critic or tax inspector in your nation has a name everyone knows. What did they do?
An ambassador has just been sent home from your capital. Whose, and what was the official reason?
A day in your calendar marks a defeat, not a victory. Why is it kept?
How do the values taught in your nation's schools show up in its art and culture?
A harvest failed in your nation last year. Of what, and what did people go without?
Your nation's war graves lie partly in someone else's country. Who tends them?
A new town in your nation was built from nothing in ten years. Who moved there, and who refused?
What does it cost to get married, to be buried and to be born in your nation? Which is dearest?
A poet in your nation is quoted by every side in every argument. Which line, and what did it mean?
Your nation gives the vote at an age its neighbours think odd. What age, and who argued for it?
Someone in your nation holds an ancient office with a fine title and no duties. What is it, and what do they do all day?
A dance in your nation was once forbidden. By whom, and where is it danced now?
A border town speaks a different language from the capital. How did that happen?
Your navy's oldest ship is retired. Who wants to keep it afloat?
Name a holiday only your nation celebrates, and the food that goes with it.
A trade route your nation depends on closes overnight. What do people buy instead?
Your nation's capital moved two centuries ago. Why, and who still resents it?
Your nation's longest tunnel, bridge or road joins two places that had managed without it. What changed when it opened?
How do people in your nation greet a friend, a stranger and a superior? What goes wrong when they mix them up?
A scientist in your nation refused a prize. Which prize, and why?
Electricity in your nation comes mostly from one source. Which, and what happens when it fails?
The armed forces run something that has nothing to do with war: a bakery, an airline, a football club. What, and why?
The place where your nation's three largest regions meet is marked by something. What, and who visits?
What is sold at a street corner in your nation that is sold nowhere else?
